about.title: Hemet Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Florida Avenue carries much of Hemet's daily traffic, and the public record shows it. In 2025, the city logged 273 injury collisions, with 419 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Florida Avenue, State Street, Stetson Avenue, and Sanderson Avenue account for the largest share of those reports, and Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. show the highest concentration. Behind each count is a person trying to sort out medical bills, a damaged car, and an insurer who wants a quick answer. We handle car accident claims for drivers in that moment. We work on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, but claims involving a city or county vehicle can be limited to six months. Waiting also lets evidence fade. A conversation now costs nothing and can clarify what your next step should be.

items.title: Contingency Fees, Nothing Up Front
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay a fee only if your car accident claim produces a recovery, and your initial consultation is always free.

items.title: Deadlines Are Watched Closely
items.desc: California allows two years for most car accident claims, but a crash involving a city, county, or state vehicle can cut that window to six months. An early consult helps you avoid missing either one.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some blame, with damages reduced by your percentage. We also help you preserve dashcam footage, photos, and witness details before they disappear.

items.question: I was hit near Florida Avenue and Sanderson Avenue in Hemet. Should I speak with the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may ask questions designed to shift fault or minimize your injuries. Report the crash to your own carrier as your policy requires, and let us handle communication with the other side. That corridor sees a high volume of reported collisions, so intersection cameras and nearby business footage may also be worth preserving quickly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Riverside County?
items.answer: For most crashes in Hemet, California gives you two years from the date of the collision to file a lawsuit. If a government vehicle or agency is involved, such as a city or county truck, you may have as little as six months to file a formal claim. Medical records and repair estimates take time to gather, so starting early protects your options.

items.question: What if the police report says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: A police report is one piece of evidence, not the final word, and California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your share of fault as determined in the claim. We can review the report, gather additional evidence, and challenge conclusions that do not match what actually happened.
